reader.requirement: At --std 85, when a GENERATE or TERMINATE in a contained program presents a report group, exactly one USE BEFORE REPORTING declarative runs: the one in the program containing the statement, else a GLOBAL one in the directly containing program, repeated outward to the outermost program; a non-GLOBAL declarative of a container, or any declarative of a contained program, is never selected, and if none qualifies none runs.

passes DialectLevel as ReportWriter.Edition for the engine's DialectBehavior questions (SUM size error, GROUP INDICATE, TERMINATE save, CF prior values); none reaches the selector chain

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|CobolVersion|Dialect|ConstructRegistry' over ReportWriterEmitter.cs, DispatchEmitter.cs, Runtime/IO/ReportWriter.cs, ReportSectionBinder.cs; ChainSelects / EmitBeforeReportingSelectors / EmitSelectors contain no edition read, so the precedence walk is the same code at every edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb369_global_report_use_selection covers a) own-beats-container, a non-GLOBAL container declarative skipped, and an outward walk two levels to the declaring program; it does not exercise an intermediate container's GLOBAL declarative winning over the outermost's GLOBAL one (only the first is run), nor a statement in the outer program ignoring a contained program's GLOBAL declarative.

reader.notes: Each unit emits a per-report selector that tries its own declaratives (any for its own statements, GLOBAL only when reached from a contained program) and otherwise delegates to __outer, stopping at the declaring program; the probe shows the intermediate GLOBAL declarative wins and the outer one is not run in addition. The only edition reads near the path govern a USE body's exit filter and engine behaviours, not the selection.

refuter.evidence: r4sib.cob at --std 85 (refute-1985-033/r4sib-001), aimed at what u1prec did not try: precedence follows CONTAINMENT, not the call chain. A (declares GLOBAL RD R-1; non-GLOBAL USE for DET-1, GLOBAL USE for DET-2) directly contains COMMON siblings B (GLOBAL USE for DET-1 and CF FINAL) and C (non-GLOBAL own USE for DET-2); A calls B, B calls C. Printed 'A-NG DET-1 N=1 / B-G DET-1 N=2 / C GEN DET-1 / C GEN DET-2 / C-NG DET-2 N=3 / C TERMINATE / C END / A DONE': C's GENERATE DET-1 ran no declarative (A's non-GLOBAL skipped by 1b, the calling sibling B's GLOBAL one never examined, 1c none executed); C's own non-GLOBAL declarative is selected by 1a and A's GLOBAL DET-2 is not also run; C's TERMINATE ran no CF FINAL declarative (sibling B's GLOBAL one not selected). cite.py: OK §1985:X.5.6.4 GR1, GR1b, GR1c (each 'the text is in').
